answer: The strongest lever is simple: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because karst only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, garden is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any wander approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
